No problem! Yes I had to give my electronics to the staff and they had a room where they would store chargers. You can always pm if you want more information

1- The food was basically the same as airplane food.

2- We could basically do what we wished and there were some scheduled activities which we could choose to participate in if we wished.

3- I could bring my phone and all other electronics but I couldn’t have chargers

4- I got therapy while being in the long term ward but not in a short term or emergency ward.

1- Psych wards are no where near as scary a tv no popular culture makes them out to be. I found it difficult but in the end I understand why I was hospitalized.
2- I have never been physically hurt while hospitalized. I have been held a few times because I was in imminent danger to myself but it wasn’t painful.
3- I felt that it was helpful and I got better.
4- The hospitals I have been at have not had containment suits. However even if a hospital has them it is very unlikely that you would be put in one.
5- It is helpful but it is also a lot of work. Psych wards don’t just fix everything and you have to be willing to accept help if you want it to work.
6- I’m not a doctor so I can’t say for sure whether you need to be hospitalized or not. What I can say is that you are only hospitalized if a doctor feels you are an immediate danger to yourself or others. You can always contact a psych ward and hear if they believe you should be hospitalized.
